transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. Before we get started, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess I’m here because people keep telling me I’m “reading too much into things,” but I don’t think I am. It’s about my father’s death, and the records around it. The hospital records, the donation emails—everyone says they line up, but when I actually compare the timestamps and notice the missing attachments, it doesn’t add up.

And then there’s the way certain people in the community avoid my questions. I work with systems, so I notice when information doesn’t match. I’m not trying to make a scene or anything, but it feels obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened.
Have you ever heard voices, seen things, or had other unusual sensory experiences that other people don't seem to notice?

Not really, no. I mean, I don’t hear voices or see things like that, if that’s what you mean.

It’s more that I notice patterns in the records—like email timing, file names, gaps where something should be. I know that sounds dry, but that’s kind of my job, noticing when systems don’t match. So no, it’s not like I’m seeing things other people can’t see. It’s just… they don’t seem to look closely enough.
Before your father passed away, would you say you generally trusted people and their motives, or have you tended to be suspicious and guarded with others for as long as you can remember?

I don’t think I was always like this, no. I mean, I’ve always been the kind of person who checks things carefully—at work if you don’t check logs and timestamps, you miss the whole problem—but I wouldn’t say I went around suspecting everyone.

This really started after my father died, when I was going through his records and messages. So… about nine months now, I guess. That’s when I started noticing things that didn’t fit. Before that, I wasn’t sitting around thinking people had motives or anything.

Since your father passed away, have you experienced repeated distressing memories, nightmares, or flashbacks about the events surrounding his death that intrude on your thoughts even when you don't want them to?

I don’t know if I’d call them flashbacks. I mean, I think about it a lot, sure, but it’s more because I’m trying to make sense of the paperwork and the sequence of things. Like when something doesn’t line up in a system, it kind of keeps running in the back of your mind until you find the error.

Nightmares… not really that I can point to. I sleep badly sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’m reliving it or anything. It’s more like I get stuck going over details, and then I remember some unrelated thing—like who sent which email, or where I saved a file—and then I’m up checking again.
Aside from your concerns about your father’s records, how are things going in the rest of your life—are you still able to keep up with work, relationships, and daily responsibilities as usual?

Mostly, yes. I mean, I’m still going to work, still handling my projects. Nobody’s had to, like, step in and take over for me. Bills get paid, groceries, laundry, all the boring things.

It’s not like everything fell apart. The issue is more when I try to talk to my family—or even a couple people from the community who knew my dad—about what I’m seeing in the records. Then people get tense, or they act like I’m making it into something it isn’t. And that becomes… frustrating. But day to day, I’m functioning. I just don’t think everyone wants to look at the details.
Since your father passed away, have you noticed a persistent low or depressed mood, or a loss of interest and pleasure in things you used to enjoy?

I’m not sure I’d call it depressed, exactly. I mean, it’s been a lot, obviously, but I still do things. I’ll still mess around with a side project or watch something, though sometimes I pause it because I remember I meant to check a folder name or some old backup location.

So… I don’t know. I haven’t really noticed losing interest in everything. It’s more like my attention gets pulled somewhere else. Does that count?
